title: Validation of a quality of life questionnaire for adolescents and young adults (14-39 years) with cancer
official: International field study to test the reliability and validity of the EORTC adolescent and young adult module (the EORTC QLQ-AYA30) for assessing health-related quality of life of adolescents and young adults with cancer
summary:
Background and study aims
A diagnosis of cancer can affect many areas of a person's life. For adolescents and young adults aged 14 to 39 years, cancer may be especially disruptive because it occurs during a period of major life transitions such as education, employment, relationships and family planning. Researchers have developed a new questionnaire, called the EORTC QLQ-AYA30, to measure quality of life specifically in young people with cancer. This study aims to assess whether the questionnaire is acceptable to patients and whether it reliably and accurately measures quality of life in this age group.

Who can participate?
People aged 14 to 39 years with any type of cancer can participate if they are currently receiving treatment, have completed treatment within the past year, or are receiving palliative care. Participants must be aware of their diagnosis and be willing and able to provide informed consent or assent. Parents or guardians will be involved in the consent process for participants under 16 years of age.

What does the study involve?
Participants will complete a general cancer quality-of-life questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30) and the adolescent and young adult cancer questionnaire being evaluated (EORTC QLQ-AYA30). They will also be asked to identify up to three important symptoms or problems and rate the impact of these on their lives, answer a question about treatment side effects, and provide feedback about the questionnaires. Feedback includes whether any questions are confusing, upsetting, or missing important issues. Some participants will be asked to complete the questionnaires again after approximately 2 weeks, 6 weeks, or at the end of treatment. Questionnaires can be completed online or on paper. Additional demographic and clinical information will also be collected.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participants may not receive any direct benefit from taking part. However, their contribution will help researchers develop and validate a questionnaire that better captures the experiences and quality of life of adolescents and young adults with cancer. Some questions may cover sensitive topics and could cause discomfort or distress, but participants can choose not to answer any question and may withdraw from the study at any time without affecting their care.

Where is the study run from?
The study is coordinated by the University of Southampton, UK, and is being conducted internationally with young people with cancer from multiple countries.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
The study is expected to begin recruiting participants in November 2026 and is planned to continue until November 2028.

Who is funding the study?
The study is funded by the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) Quality of Life Group.

Who is the main contact?
Professor Anne-Sophie Darlington,  School of Health Sciences, University of Southampton, a.darlington@soton.ac.uk.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age between 14 years and 39 years (inclusive) at the time of study enrolment
2. Confirmed diagnosis of cancer of any type, stage, and including those with recurrence or a secondary cancer
3. Aware of diagnosis
4. Undergoing treatment (any type) for cancer with curative or palliative intent
5. Completed treatment for cancer within the past 12 months
6. Receiving palliative support for incurable disease
7. Willing and able to give fully informed consent or assent (participants below the age of having legal capacity to consent, in the UK this is 16 years)
8. Willingness and ability of a parent/guardian to give fully informed consent for their child to participate if aged before 16 years
Exclusion criteria:
1. Unable to give fully informed consent (or assent even if the parent/guardian consents)
2. Unwilling to give informed consent (or assent even if the parent/guardian consents)
3. Participated in Phase 1-3 of the development of the EORTC QLQ-AYA30
4. Completed treatment for cancer > 12 months and no evidence of active disease
5. On maintenance treatment and no evidence of active disease
